steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: CPU: ALU (arithmetic/logic), CU (control signals), Registers: PC (next instruction), ACC (results), MAR (address), MDR (data), CIR (instruction), SR (flags)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: FDE: Fetch (PC to MAR, memory to MDR/CIR, PC++), Decode (CU interprets CIR), Execute (ALU/control)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Pipelining: fetch/decode/execute overlap; hazards (data, control, structural)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Memory: Registers > L1 cache > L2 > L3 > RAM > SSD > HDD; Virtual memory: paging, page table, TLB, page fault

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: A program has 20 percent serial code. Max speedup on 4 cores? --- Solution: Amdahl: speedup = 1/((1-0.8) + 0.8/4) = 1/(0.2 + 0.2) = 2.5x. Even infinite cores: 1/0.2 = 5x

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: List registers and their purposes | Draw FDE cycle diagram | Explain cache hit/miss

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of computer systems and architecture with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: A program has 20 percent serial code. Max speedup on 4 cores?. Solution: Amdahl: speedup = 1/((1-0.8) + 0.8/4) = 1/(0.2 + 0.2) = 2.5x. Even infinite cores: 1/0.2 = 5x Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice questions independently; circulate and support. Plenary (5 min): Review answers and address misconceptions.

steps.title: Homework
steps.body: List registers and their purposes Draw FDE cycle diagram Explain cache hit/miss Compare CISC vs RISC Calculate speedup: 30 percent serial, 8 cores
